set: A: the page at rest, its result, and eight of the keys, as a web page

issues.where: the assessment introduction and the intake on the right
issues.what: The first screen explains why there is an assessment but gives no instruction or recognizable way to start it. The intake looks like an illustration, and the tube leaving the frame is the only clue that anything follows.
issues.fix: Put a clearly labeled Start assessment action directly below the intro and let it trigger the intake gag. Give the resting page an explicit route to the result if the sequence does not play.

issues.where: the wide reveal of the pinball table
issues.what: The table and its tubes look physically coherent, but the isolated cabinet on black reads as a separate scene rather than a mechanism coming out of the application page. The visible tube in the prior page frame has no recognizable junction here.
issues.fix: At the wide reveal, retain a sliver of the application surface with the circular intake or show a clearly matching tube joint. Save the fully isolated black framing for the following close-ups.

issues.where: the Background Check sign above the right-hand ramp
issues.what: The rail crosses the label and obscures part of Background, while the neighboring station labels have clear sightlines.
issues.fix: Raise the sign above the rail crossing or place it on the unobstructed right face of the station.

issues.where: the completion message inside the gray panel
issues.what: The paragraph runs almost the full width of the panel and leaves 'in Building C.' stranded on the second line, weakening the punch line and making the result feel less finished.
issues.fix: Give the copy a narrower measure or wrap it after the first sentence so the lines are balanced and 'vending machines in Building C.' stays together.
